{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZlTIdw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDL1Uw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 99, "title": "Delay same-scanline nonzero H-only and H/V IRQ assertions by 14 master clocks", "body": "## Problem

H-only and H/V timer IRQs still assert at `HTIME * 4`, without the documented comparison-to-assertion delay. This is the unfinished scheduler behavior prioritized by the latest assessment; #97 corrected only V-only IRQs.

At baseline `20116952ce5617cc487fed33fa7c5574ed86adf0`, [`SystemBus::tick`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/20116952ce5617cc487fed33fa7c5574ed86adf0/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L195) sets the IRQ flag on the immediate horizontal crossing. Existing combined-timer tests explicitly encode that approximation. It affects TIMEUP observations, WAI wake timing and guest synchronization.

## Expected outcome

Implement the documented delay for preconfigured, nonzero H-only and H/V comparisons whose assertion remains inside the current NTSC non-interlaced scanline.

The source contract is [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm), **SNES Timing H/V Events** and **SNES PPU Interrupts**, reconciled with [Anomie's Register Doc, revision 1157](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt), **NMITIMEN**, **HTIME/VTIME** and **TIMEUP**. The repository's [#97 reconciliation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/20116952ce5617cc487fed33fa7c5574ed86adf0/docs/issue-97-validation.md#specification-and-bounded-contract) records the nonzero horizontal assertion rule as `HTIME + 3.5` timer units. Four master clocks per timer unit give:

`assertion_offset = 4 * HTIME + 14`

For this bounded behavior:

- NMITIMEN `$10`: assert once per eligible scanline, independently of VTIME.
- NMITIMEN `$30`: assert only on the VTIME-selected scanline.
- With no earlier pending IRQ, TIMEUP bit 7 remains clear before the assertion clock and becomes set at it. Preserve existing pending-flag retention and read acknowledgement.
- NMITIMEN `$20` retains #97's V-only assertion at master H=10, independently of HTIME.
- CPU interrupt recognition remains instruction-boundary behavior; scheduler assertion and CPU handler entry are distinct events.

Independent expected offsets include:

| HTIME | Assertion master clock within line |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | 18 |
| 64 | 270 |
| 256 | 1038 |
| 321 | 1298 |
| 323 | 1306 |
| 327 | 1322 |
| 336 | 1358 |
| 337 | 1362, ordinary 1364-clock lines only |

The bounded domain is nonzero HTIME with `4 * HTIME + 14 < line_length`: 1–337 on ordinary lines and 1–336 on the alternate-field short line. CPU timer units must remain distinct from the long-dot PPU counter conversion described in [#95](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/20116952ce5617cc487fed33fa7c5574ed86adf0/docs/issue-95-validation.md#specification-reconciliation-recorded-before-implementation).

### Scope and unresolved semantics

The local validation records establish the rule above but do not settle HTIME=0 or assertions extending beyond the current line. Inspect the cited specification sections before implementation and explicitly reconcile those cases with this bounded domain. Do not extrapolate a rollover rule, preserve an unsupported earlier Issue requirement as hardware fact, or use existing approximation tests as specification evidence. If a source contradicts this contract, correct the contract and numerical derivation with cited evidence before implementing it.

Zero and line-spanning comparisons remain explicitly unresolved unless that reconciliation supplies a defensible bounded correction. Avoid incidental changes to their scheduling. Their retained implementation is an approximation, not verified hardware behavior.

Other non-goals: live timer-register/enable races, physical reset timing, TIMEUP write-clear and coincident-read disputes, within-instruction CPU sampling, NMI delays, DMA startup/alignment, PAL, interlace and raster rendering.

## Context and reproduction

Repository inspection was read-only; no suites were rerun and no external specifications were freshly retrieved. HEAD matches the supplied baseline; the supplied open-Issue list is empty.

A minimal original unit reproduction can configure H/V mode with HTIME=64 and VTIME=1 before entering line 1. In field 0, line 1 starts at absolute clock 1364. The baseline asserts at 1620; the documented delayed event is 1634. Fresh observations at 1633/1634/1635 distinguish the required behavior without acknowledgement concealing a failure.

Inspect and preserve these dependent regressions:

- [`machine.rs` timer tests](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/20116952ce5617cc487fed33fa7c5574ed86adf0/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L976): re-derive nonzero combined-timer and rollover expectations; separate zero-case approximation controls.
- [`tests/ntsc_timing.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/20116952ce5617cc487fed33fa7c5574ed86adf0/crates/snes-core/tests/ntsc_timing.rs): its HTIME=321 guest currently derives captures from immediate comparison. Preserve counter geometry and four natural fields while correcting the timing derivation.
- [`tests/ppu_counter_latch.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/20116952ce5617cc487fed33fa7c5574ed86adf0/crates/snes-core/tests/ppu_counter_latch.rs): re-derive captures affected by delayed HTIME=256 wake.
- [`tests/ppu_oam_reload.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/20116952ce5617cc487fed33fa7c5574ed86adf0/crates/snes-core/tests/ppu_oam_reload.rs): its HTIME=330 wake intentionally places the first OAM read before VBlank H=40. Retime the original guest to preserve that distinction; merely accepting an after-reload observation would remove its regression coverage.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record the source reconciliation, exact timer-unit arithmetic, bounded domain and unresolved zero/late cases in validation documentation. Update superseded timing statements and relevant provenance derivations; distinguish documented facts from emulator access/sampling conventions.
- [ ] Implement the delayed same-line assertion for both H-only and H/V modes. Preserve V-only timing, scanline lengths, field reporting, pending acknowledgement and device advancement.
- [ ] Add original independent unit vectors covering the table above, fresh before/at/after observations, acknowledgement without duplicate same-line assertion, pending retention, H-only VTIME independence, H/V nonmatching lines and unreachable VTIME values. Exercise V=0/1/224/225/239/240/241/261 across both field parities through natural rollover. Do not obtain expected clocks from production timing helpers.
- [ ] Verify one-clock, irregular and whole-interval advancement across ordinary/short-line and field boundaries. Include timed CPU TIMEUP reads and real general-DMA reads around a corrected assertion, plus deferred CPU IRQ service during DMA. Label access-end and DMA-phase expectations as existing model conventions.
- [ ] Add an original source-built, self-checking 65C816 diagnostic exercising both horizontal modes across natural fields, with literal independently derived observations, guest success/failure markers and bounded execution. The host must not inject beam, IRQ or result state. Document authorship, license and construction in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`.
- [ ] Demonstrate behavioral assertion failures for the new boundary regression and diagnostic on the exact baseline with only test sources/harness registration transferred. Compilation failures do not count. Record executable focused-test commands and passing corrected results.
- [ ] Preserve the existing hardware regressions identified above, including the OAM pre/post-H=40 distinction. Change timing-dependent guest setup or literals only with independent arithmetic; retain their original hardware assertions and coverage.
- [ ] Pass `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --workspace --locked`. This includes V-only IRQ, NTSC geometry, CPU interrupt/WAI, controllers, DMA/HDMA, PPU ports and audio regressions.
- [ ] Run the existing source-built hardware gates from [README validation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/20116952ce5617cc487fed33fa7c5574ed86adf0/README.md#validate):

```sh
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
```

- [ ] Build the cleared games twice, rebuild actual Wasm/browser artifacts and pass the mandatory browser suite:

```sh
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
npm --prefix web exec playwright install chromium
npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
```

Use the README compiler override or alternate test port where necessary. Preserve source/tool/game pins, licenses, ROM hashes, replay routes, gameplay/progression/music assertions and tolerances. Use only original or existing audited licensed source-built fixtures; acquire no commercial ROM or firmware. Report actual failures, passes and unavailable checks.

### Remaining inventory

This Issue does not complete `scheduler`: zero/late IRQs, live configuration, NMI delays, refresh/startup revisions, CPU sampling and broader synchronization remain outstanding.

Retain all 24 inventory categories and their existing scope: `cpu`, `bus`, `scheduler`, `dma`, `hdma`, `controllers`, `ppu-bg`, `ppu-offset`, `ppu-hires`, `ppu-mode7`, `ppu-objects`, `ppu-color`, `ppu-ports`, `ppu-display`, `spc`, `ipl`, `dsp-voices`, `dsp-noise`, `dsp-pitch`, `dsp-envelope`, `dsp-echo` and `dsp-timing` remain partial; `ppu-raster` and `pal` remain unimplemented. None is fully verified. Limited passing tests establish neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility, and do not complete Issue #3.

## Optional validation

Physical-device corroboration and the existing optional 301-second real-time browser soaks, using only appropriately licensed available artifacts. Neither blocks this bounded correction.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
